 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti

Judgment:

This appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed by the District Judge-cum- Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mahabubnagar in O.P.No.168 of 2005 dated 13.06.2008.
2.

entities.text: District Judge-cum- Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and learned counsel for the claimant and perused the entire material available on record.

3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of damages to the load of Sunflower oil while transporting the same in Eicher vehicle from Wanaparthy to Hyderabad.
4. The case of the claimant is that on 17.10.2004, the loaded 50 quintals 10 kgs of Sunflower oil in a tanker in Eicher vehicle at Crescent mill, Wanaparthy to transport the same to Hyderabad.

While the driver of the vehicle stopped it on left side of the road, the driver of the lorry while coming from Kurnool side drove it in rash and negligent manner, in high speed and dashed the stationed Eicher vehicle from its back side, due to which the pipe of the tanker LK, J MACMA_4487_2008 damaged resulting in leakage of total sun flower oil causing loss of Rs.2,00,400/-.

5. It is the case of the Insurance Company that they are not liable to pay the damages as claimed by the petitioner at Rs.3,00,000/- and as per the damage of property the Insurance Company is liable to pay the maximum of Rs.6,000/-.

The Tribunal while considering this issue has observed that it is the evidence of RW-1 that the respondent No.2 collected premium of Rs.3,630/- under third party claim and the tariff is applicable in this case.

It is also evidence of RW-1 that the third party property damage does not covers contents of the vehicle, but the Ex.B-1 does not disclose that the liability of third party property damage is not covered to the contents of the vehicle.
In view of the same, the Tribunal has held that the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.7,50,000/-.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the liability of the Insurance Company is limited to Rs.6,000/- and this aspect was not considered by the tribunal.
The tribunal has observed that the Insurance policy does not contain the same.

It is submitted that without any basis, the Tribunal has granted the compensation and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay The National Insurance Company Limited vs Mohd. Jameel Ahmed on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34997217/
1 the same.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Mohd. Jameel Ahmed on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Counsel appearing for the respondent/ claimant submits that as the vehicle is insured and because of the use of the vehicle the goods which were in the vehicle were damaged, as such the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation.
8. This Court is not able to appreciate the contention raised on behalf of respondent/claimant.
It is damage to the property but not to the person and for that the liability of the Insurance Company is only Rs.6,000/- as per the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
9. Accordingly, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the Insurance Company shall pay only an amount of Rs.6,000/-.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
